question: How many days of annual leave do I get after my probation ends?
answer: After completing probation, full-time employees receive 20 working days of paid annual leave per calendar year, rising to 25 working days once you have more than 5 years of continuous service. If you are part-time, your leave is in proportion to your contracted hours. Public holidays are in addition to this leave.

question: How many unused leave days can I carry over into next year, and when do I have to use them?
answer: You can carry over up to 5 unused annual leave days into the next calendar year, and you must use them by 31 March or they are lost. Any days above the 5-day limit are lost at the end of the year unless the Head of People approves an exception in writing.

question: Which days am I expected to be in the office?
answer: If you're in a hybrid role, you're expected in the Lagos office on Tuesday and Thursday, which are anchor days. Overall, hybrid employees work from the office at least 2 days per week. Other days may be worked from home if your line manager agrees.

question: How far in advance do I need to request an international trip?
answer: International travel must be requested at least 21 days before departure. If you request later than that, the request may be refused or may need Director approval.

question: What is the deadline for submitting an expense claim?
answer: You must submit expense claims in the Spendly expense tool within 30 days of the expense. Also note that approved claims submitted before the 20th of the month are paid with that month's payroll, while claims submitted on or after the 20th are paid in the following month's payroll.

question: I lost my work laptop. What should I do?
answer: Report the lost laptop to IT Support (it-support@kestrelnova.example) within 24 hours; IT will remotely lock and wipe the device. If the laptop was stolen rather than lost, you must also report the theft to the police and share the report reference with IT.

question: What is my yearly budget for training and courses?
answer: As a permanent employee, you have a learning budget of NGN 400,000 per calendar year, which covers courses, certifications, conferences and books. Any unused budget does not carry over to the next year.

question: How much paternity leave do I get?
answer: You get 10 working days of paternity leave at full pay. You must take it within 3 months of your child's birth or adoption, and you can split it into up to two blocks.

question: A supplier sent me a gift worth NGN 25,000. Can I keep it?
answer: Not automatically. NGN 25,000 is above the NGN 15,000 limit, so you must declare the gift to Compliance (compliance@kestrelnova.example) within 5 working days. Compliance will then decide whether you may keep it, return it or donate it. If the gift is cash, a voucher or a gift card, you must not accept it at all, whatever its value.

question: I stayed in a hotel costing NGN 70,000 per night on a domestic work trip. Is that within the limit, and who needs to approve my claim?
answer: Yes. NGN 70,000 per night is within the domestic hotel limit of NGN 80,000 per night. Because the amount is above NGN 50,000, your claim needs approval from both your line manager and Finance.

question: The company paid NGN 300,000 for my certification. If I resign 8 months after finishing it, what do I owe, and what happens to my unused annual leave?
answer: Your certification cost NGN 300,000, which is more than the NGN 200,000 threshold. You would be resigning within 12 months of completing it, so you must repay 50% of the cost: NGN 150,000. This will be deducted from your final salary where possible. Any accrued but unused annual leave for the current year will be paid out at your basic daily rate in your final salary. However, if you have taken more leave than you accrued, the excess will be deducted from your final salary.
